hunt.justification: AI agents move data far faster than humans, rendering traditional manual monitoring ineffective; a negative result ensures that autonomous exfiltration is not occurring under the guise of AI productivity.

meta.name: Autonomous AI Agent and Shadow AI Activity

related.reason: This hunt focuses on the behavioral footprint of AI agents, not the prompt injection techniques used to manipulate them.

meta.analysis: A single rule might fire on a Tor connection, but this hunt correlates vulnerability state, proxy sign-ins, and machine-speed API counts across three different telemetry surfaces to detect novel 'synthetic insider' patterns.

stages.name: AI-Accelerated Initial Access
observables: Exploitation of public-facing web applications or hypervisors
Signs of identity fraud in sign-in events using AI-generated media
Onboarding of fraudulent 'fake candidates' with legitimate internal access

stages.name: Multi-hop Proxy Anonymization
observables: Network connections routed through chained proxies or Tor-gateways
DNS lookups for .onion domains or known tor-to-web services
Traffic masking origin of automated AI reconnaissance tools

stages.name: AI Agent Post-Breach Activity
observables: Autonomous AI agents executing system actions without human approval
API activity from LLM integration keys moving data at superhuman velocity
Synthetic insiders behaving like legitimate users but with excessive permissions

stages.name: Exfiltration via Shadow AI
observables: HTTP requests to unauthorized LLM providers (api.openai.com, anthropic.com)
Pasting sensitive IP or PII into unapproved chat-based AI domains
Large data uploads to unmonitored third-party AI infrastructure

scenario.summary: Adversaries leverage AI-accelerated zero-day exploitation and automated hiring fraud to secure legitimate access to corporate environments. Once inside, they deploy autonomous AI agents as 'synthetic insiders' to move data at machine speed, exfiltrating sensitive intellectual property through unapproved shadow AI tools and LLM prompts over multi-hop proxy infrastructure.

meta.rationale: Begin with internet-facing systems reporting critical vulnerabilities. The velocity query is most effective in cloud control-plane environments where automated agents reside.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary is using AI-assisted exploitation or fraudulent identity onboarding to gain initial access, followed by the deployment of automated synthetic insiders that move data to unauthorized LLM providers at machine speed.

ai_domains.description: Domains of third-party AI/LLM providers to monitor for shadow AI activity.

scope_hosts.description: Specific hostnames to focus on; leave empty to hunt across the entire estate.

proxy_gateways.description: Known Tor-to-web gateways used to anonymize traffic.

references.name: Proofpoint — The Hidden AI Security Risks Threatening Businesses

blind_spots.risk: Cloud logging latency (e.g., CloudTrail) may allow an agent to finish exfiltrating data before the hunt can observe the velocity spikes.
blind_spots.question: How quickly can we see the machine-speed actions of an AI agent?

blind_spots.risk: Without TLS decryption, the hunt can see the destination and the size of the upload but cannot confirm the classification of the data.
blind_spots.question: What content was in the request body to the AI provider?
blind_spots.requires: Endpoint TLS decryption or HTTP inspection

hunt.name: Autonomous AI Agent and Shadow AI Activity
hunt.description: This hunt identifies the emergence of synthetic insiders and shadow AI usage. It follows a phased approach: first scoping internet-facing vulnerabilities and identifying multi-hop proxy evasion or proxy-based sign-ins. The second phase pivots to detect superhuman API velocity and data movement to unauthorized AI platforms. An agentic triage correlates early access indicators with behavioral exfiltration patterns to identify autonomous threats.

config.scoping_notes: Begin with internet-facing systems reporting critical vulnerabilities. The velocity query is most effective in cloud control-plane environments where automated agents reside.
config.beyond_detection: A single rule might fire on a Tor connection, but this hunt correlates vulnerability state, proxy sign-ins, and machine-speed API counts across three different telemetry surfaces to detect novel 'synthetic insider' patterns.

config.content: SELECT device_uid, resource_uid, cve_uid, severity, title FROM hb_vulnerability_finding WHERE severity_id >= 4 AND status != 'suppressed' ORDER BY severity_id DESC
config.description: Scope the hunt to devices with high or critical vulnerabilities that are susceptible to initial access exploits.
config.expected_signal: A list of device UIDs and associated high-severity vulnerabilities. This step provides the context of exposure for the estate.

primitive_config.label: Identify vulnerable internet-facing assets
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_uid, resource_uid, cve_uid, severity, title FROM hb_vulnerability_finding WHERE severity_id >= 4 AND status != 'suppressed' ORDER BY severity_id DESC
primitive_config.expected: A list of device UIDs and associated high-severity vulnerabilities. This step provides the context of exposure for the estate.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, actor_user_name, query_hostname, process_name, COUNT(*) as lookup_count FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{proxy_gateways}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, actor_user_name, query_hostname, process_name
config.description: Identify hosts using gateways to mask their connection to dark web resources or C2 infrastructure.
config.expected_signal: Rare DNS queries for gateways like onion.pet. Silence proves no gateways were resolved during the window.

primitive_config.label: DNS lookups for Tor-to-web gateways
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, actor_user_name, query_hostname, process_name, COUNT(*) as lookup_count FROM hb_dns_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{proxy_gateways}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(query_hostname) || ',') > 0) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY device_hostname, actor_user_name, query_hostname, process_name
primitive_config.expected: Rare DNS queries for gateways like onion.pet. Silence proves no gateways were resolved during the window.

config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, src_endpoint_ip, src_location_country, device_hostname, is_proxy, status FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE is_proxy = 'true' AND status_id = 1 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify users logging in via known anonymizers, suggesting bypass of location-based controls or identity fraud.
config.expected_signal: Successful logons where is_proxy is true. This marks potentially fraudulent identities or sessions.

primitive_config.label: Proxy-based sign-in anomalies
primitive_config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, src_endpoint_ip, src_location_country, device_hostname, is_proxy, status FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE is_proxy = 'true' AND status_id = 1 AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: Successful logons where is_proxy is true. This marks potentially fraudulent identities or sessions.

config.objective: Determine if vulnerabilities and proxy usage indicate a legitimate security incident or identity risk.
config.description: Determine if the scoped hosts and evasion indicators represent a credible threat beachhead.
config.expected_signal: A list of high-risk users and hosts to carry forward into behavioral analysis.
config.success_criteria: A per-host verdict of suspicious | benign citing specific vulnerabilities or proxy logons.

config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, api_operation, strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H', time) AS hour, COUNT(*) as op_count FROM hb_cloud_api_activity WHERE time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY actor_user_name, api_operation, hour HAVING op_count > 500 ORDER BY op_count DESC
config.description: Find principals executing operations at a frequency that suggests automated AI agents rather than human users.
config.expected_signal: Users with hundreds of API calls in a single hour, indicating an automated synthetic insider.

primitive_config.label: Superhuman API activity velocity
primitive_config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, api_operation, strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H', time) AS hour, COUNT(*) as op_count FROM hb_cloud_api_activity WHERE time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY actor_user_name, api_operation, hour HAVING op_count > 500 ORDER BY op_count DESC
primitive_config.expected: Users with hundreds of API calls in a single hour, indicating an automated synthetic insider.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, actor_user_name, url_hostname, url_path, http_method, request_body_len FROM hb_http_activity WHERE (instr(',' || '{{ai_domains}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(url_hostname) || ',') > 0) AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') ORDER BY request_body_len DESC
config.description: Identify large data transfers to unauthorized third-party LLM providers.
config.expected_signal: Rows indicating significant uploads to OpenAI or Anthropic endpoints. Silence suggests no traffic to these specific domains.

config.objective: Determine if the identified principals are behaving as automated malicious agents and if exfiltration to AI providers has occurred.

config.success_criteria: A verdict of malicious for principals that exhibit both anomalous access and automated behavioral patterns.
